We got search results. The first entry seems relevant: template for aromatic bromination? The retro_smarts_template shows [Br;D1;H0:1]-[c;H0;D3;+0:2]1:[cH;... etc. That seems like a bromination template. It has template_id? The result includes reaction_id and template_hash but not template_id. The task wants template_id (the one used to search the database not the hash). Possibly the template_id is the reaction_id? Or maybe there is a separate ID. In search results, each entry has 'reaction_id' which could be template ID? Usually template ID is integer. So we can use reaction_id as template_id.

We need mapped_rxn from that template. The first entry's mapped_rxn is a long string: '[Br:1][C:2]1=[CH:3][CH:4]=[C:5]2[C:6](=[CH:7]1)[CH:8]=[CH:9][C:10]1=[C:11]2[CH:12]=[CH:13][CH:14]([Br:15])[CH2:16]1.O=C1CCC(=O)N1Br.ClC(Cl)(Cl)Cl>>[Br:1][C:2]1=[CH:3][CH:4]=[C:5]2[C:6](=[CH:7]1)[CH:8]=[CH:9][C:10]1=[C:11]2[CH:12]=[CH:13][C:14]([Br:15])=[CH:16]1'

But that seems complex with extra reagents (O=C1...). Might be not simple bromination.

Second entry maybe simpler: mapped_rxn: 'Br[Br:5].Br.[CH3:1][C:2]1=[CH:3][CH:4]=[C:6]([CH3:7])[CH:8]=[CH:9]1>>[CH3:1][C:2]1=[CH:3][C:4]([Br:5])=[C:6]([CH3:7])[CH:8]=[CH:9]1' That's also not simple.

We need a template that when applied to aromatic bromide (c1ccccc1Br) gives precursors: benzene (c1ccccc1) and Br2? The template likely breaks C-Br bond and forms H-Br? But we just need mapped_rxn.

Maybe there is a template with retro_smarts: [c:1]-[Br:2]>>[c:1]-[H].[Br:2]?? Let's search with functional_groups_broken=["aryl halide"]?
